Rules summary Contents 1 🎯 Goal 2 🔄 Round Overview 2.1 1️⃣ Plan (simultaneous) 2.2 2️⃣ Welcome (turn order) 2.3 3️⃣ Expand (turn order, optional) 2.4 4️⃣ Improve (simultaneous, optional) 2.5 5️⃣ Operate (simultaneous – main phase) 2.6 6️⃣ Upkeep (simultaneous) 3 🏁 End of Game 3.1 🧠 Key Things to Remember 🎯 Goal Score the most stars ⭐ by efficiently operating attractions in your theme park. Guests are dice: you move, modify, and exhaust them to run attractions and score points. 🔄 Round Overview The game is played over 4 rounds (or 5 in the full game ). Each round has 6 phases : 1️⃣ Plan (simultaneous) Play 2 staff cards . These determine: Turn order (lower dice total = earlier) Income (money icons) Staff abilities you can use this round 2️⃣ Welcome (turn order) Choose a monorail . Take its 3 guest dice and place them at your Park Entrance . Some staff can boost arriving dice. 3️⃣ Expand (turn order, optional) You may: Build 1 attraction (pay cost, place adjacent) Recruit 1 mascot (£5) Full game: also gain a skill card Matching amenities across your park can give instant bonuses . 4️⃣ Improve (simultaneous, optional) You may: Buy 1 map (£3) Install up to 2 upgrades : 💰 Merch kiosk → +£2 per operation ⭐ Special effect → +2⭐ per operation ⚙ Generator → operate attraction twice per round 5️⃣ Operate (simultaneous – main phase) Run your park in any order. To operate an attraction , always do these steps: Place an operate cube Assemble a party of dice that meet the attraction’s requirement Pip down all used dice (–1 each; dice at 1 are discarded) Move one used die to an adjacent attraction Helpful tools: Maps move dice between attractions Mascots adjust die value or colour (or use skills) Generators allow extra operations 👉 You don’t score immediately — everything is counted later. 6️⃣ Upkeep (simultaneous) Score stars and money from operated attractions Apply upgrade bonuses Check the round objective (mid/late game) Discard all value-1 dice Reset staff, maps, mascots, and refill monorails 🏁 End of Game Gain 1⭐ per £3 remaining Highest ⭐ wins Ties: 1️⃣ Most guest dice remaining 2️⃣ Most money 3️⃣ Shared victory 🧠 Key Things to Remember Dice wear out as you use them Moving dice is mandatory when operating Efficient chaining of attractions is the key to high scores Staff planning matters as much as park layout Nothing to see here

[Rating: 2/10] I have to compare this vs it's development brother Dice Hospital. In that regard, it was pretty disappointing. It could be that I just don't understand how to play it well after one play, but that in itself is a negative. It is just confusing as all get out. On top of that, it just plan does not look as good either. Everything feels very disjointed. (Rating based on digital play only)

[Rating: 3/10] Overly complicated, there is a game there but it needs to be better refined.  On of the admistrator cards is very over powered, can only build one attraction in a round, hard to move the Dice around, even with the map tokens.

[Rating: 3/10] Holy shit, this is awful. This one caught my interest as Dice Hospital got a lot of buzz, this seems to be rated a medium weight game, and was about building a theme park. Sounds like it should at least be interesting. The concept is about the only likable thing about the game. You start the game with an embarrassment of riches and just keep getting more and more. You have so much at your disposal that it seems impossible to NOT fully utilize every attraction in your park which completely negates most of the optimization and all of the fun; the game needed to be much more restrictive to impose

[Rating: 3/10] A game that is in need of some real development. Not a bad game at its core but it is much too long for what it is. I don't have a problem with games with very little interaction but this does not even feel like a game at all. It is more like a solo puzzle.

[Rating: 3/10] Pretty awful, very fiddly without much payoff. It has a big complicated Vlaada-esque resolution phase that takes a long time, but unlike Vlaada games resources are so plentiful that 99% of the time you get to do every possible action anyhow. Could be an OK introductory game for kids maybe, since it creates the illusion that you're puzzling through a bunch of decisions but the answers are easy enough that you will probably get them correct regardless. But even then, I don't know why you wouldn't just use a better game instead.

[Rating: 3/10] I thought I would like it because I like Dice Hospital... I was wrong.  I kept thinking I was misunderstanding something because it seemed so complex as a follow-up game.  I did not like Dice Theme Park.

[Rating: 4/10] The integration of theme is excellent - dice representing funseekers who have different levels of fitness/enthusiasm with a preference for specific rides, moving from ride to ride becoming more and more tired....excellent idea.  Throw in maps and mascots to give the player more control and you'd think this was a winner. ...  Not so, it's very solitaire with a lot of personal housekeeping and very easy to make an innocent mistake.  A lot of moving parts mean this just isn't that much fun.

[Rating: 4/10] This is Dice Hospital++, but not in a good way.  It has a bunch of phases over 5 rounds, that ends up boiling down to a massive multi-player solitaire phase where everyone has their head down running their "engine", hoping someone isn't cheating by making an accidental error.  If you really love DH then give this one a try, it is more of what you already like.  But if you do not enjoy DH, I would skip this one.

[Rating: 4/10] Not very good:  1. The core of the game - figuring out how to move the dice around to optimize your earnings each round - is decent, but  2. There's too much other stuff going on, and  3. The core puzzle is not actually that difficult once you get the hang of it. I understand why it was not made more difficult - there's no way you can reset your turn (unless you're playing on BGA) so if the puzzle is made too hard people will tend to get very frustrated when they make mistakes and want to back up. However, it means that the game outstays its welcome.
